named_events.loss_description: exceptional impact of COVID-19, primarily on contingency class where the Syndicate had exposure to events cancellation risks. In addition to direct losses, the Syndicate has given due consideration to future recessionary impact on the reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross reserve strengthening of GBP 13.801 million for prior underwriting years (2016, 2017, and 2018), representing 7.27% of its opening gross reserves. This adverse development is attributed to the exceptional impact of COVID-19, particularly on contingency class, and the consideration of future recessionary impacts on reserves. Underlying liability estimates are influenced by assumptions regarding claims development patterns, average claim costs, handling costs, inflation factors, and claim numbers, with qualitative judgements applied for market factors, public attitude to claiming, economic conditions, portfolio mix, policy conditions, claims handling procedures, judicial decisions, and government legislation.

given due consideration to future recessionary impact on the reserves
The measurement of the provision for claims outstanding involves judgements and assumptions about the future
The ultimate cost of outstanding claims is estimated using a range of techniques including actuarial and statistical projections, benchmarking, case by case review and judgement

The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience. This includes assumptions in respect of average claim costs, claim handling costs, claim inflation factors and claim numbers for each underwriting year.

Additional qualitative judgements are used to assess the extent to which past trends may not apply in the future, for example: once-off occurrence; changes in market factors such as public attitude to claiming; economic conditions; as well as internal factors such as portfolio mix, policy conditions and claims handling procedures.
Judgement is further used to assess the extent to which external factors such as judicial decisions and government legislation affect the estimates.
